summary: Hopkins County, KY fire tower in use in 1947; a 1957 notice says the Charleston Tower replaced an old wooden structure east of Beulah. Site today not described.

events.note: Dawson Springs Progress notice (Nov. 28, 1947) describes a fire tower located at Beulah, in use for detection in the eastern part of Caldwell County
Dawson Springs Progress notice (Oct. 3, 1957) says the Charleston Tower replaced the old wooden structure formerly east of Beulah on Highway 70; the notice does not name the Beulah tower

evidence.supports: 1947 notice: fire tower at Beulah, Hopkins County, good observation for the eastern part of Caldwell County
evidence.quote: A fire tower located at Beulah, in Hopkins County, affords excellent observation for detection of fire in the eastern part of Caldwell County.

evidence.supports: 1957 notice: Charleston Tower replaces the old wooden structure formerly east of Beulah on Highway 70
evidence.quote: The Charleston Tower replaces the old wooden structure formerly located east of Beulah on Highway 70.

evidence.supports: new tower twenty feet taller than the old one
evidence.quote: The new tower is twenty feet higher

sources.title: Beulah Heights, Forest Lookouts (quoting The Dawson Springs Progress, 1947 and 1957)

notes_for_editor: Only source is the Forest Lookouts Beulah page quoting two Dawson Springs Progress notices. Whether the 1947 Beulah tower is the old wooden structure the 1957 notice describes is an inference, not stated in any source. The Charleston story (us-ky-charleston) covers the 1957 replacement and should stay consistent with this one. The Kentucky index marks Beulah with an asterisk and gives no key for it. Record has no status, staffing or access; two web searches found no further source and nothing describing the site today.
